title: Answer to Question: The Hot Conflict in Turkey between the Kemalist Secularists of the English and the Liberal Secularists of America
text:
Answer to Question

The Hot Conflict in Turkey between the Kemalist Secularists of the English and the Liberal Secularists of America

Question: What is this that is going on in Turkey? A presidential election in parliament, then an election by the people, then parliamentary elections, striking movements in the circles of the army and the government, statements and counter-statements, the Constitutional Court entering the line, and the President of the Republic's approval and non-approval... And what is the role of the American-British struggle in the matter? And does the Kurdistan party have a role, especially as actions of bombing and the like have been noticed and attributed to it during this melee, and we know that it is America that established it? And finally, how is the balance of power of the Turkish parties in the parliamentary elections next month?

Answer:

For the picture to become clear, it is necessary to go back to the history of the emergence of secular Turkey:

First: Ever since the criminal Mustafa Kemal implemented the schemes of the English by destroying the Khilafah after the First World War, he proceeded against Islam, its thoughts and its sentiments, and proceeded on a (secular) line more spiteful against Islam and the Muslims than the secularists themselves. He and his clique were also keen to make Turkey a pillar for Britain in the region. That is, he proceeded on two lines which he made his method:

Fighting Islam, and loyalty to Britain.

It continued like this until America came out into the world after the Second World War, exploiting its victory to be the first, dominant state replacing the former colonialism (Britain and France) in their colonies. Hence there was the meeting of America's ambassadors in the Middle East in Istanbul in 1950.

America tried earnestly to penetrate Turkey by infiltrating the army, which it sees as the effective force holding the reins of the country, but it could not, for the army is saturated with the method of Mustafa Kemal (the Englishman). So it saw that the only means before it was to resort to drawing close to the sentiments of the Muslims, who resent the army and the secularists. Thus it was in the fifties with Adnan Menderes, in the eighties with Özal, and between them in the seventies and then in the nineties with Demirel, although at the end of his era he came to master the game of tug-of-war between America and the English. In any case, America collided each time with a coup by the army against the government whenever America's agents crossed not the red lines but even the yellow lines, or came close to them! Thus the army carried out the coups of 1960, 1971, 1980 and 1997, their pretext each time being the preservation of the (English) secular system).

America learned something new from each coup. It became convinced of the impossibility of infiltrating the army, so in Özal's era it tried to create a parallel force, and Özal began arming the police with strong armament. It should be known that he had clear Islamic sentiments about him, for he was of the Naqshbandi tariqah, which made him beloved by the general Muslims. But he was not content with the premiership in 1983; rather, he became President of the Republic in 1989, and this is a sensitive position for the secularists and the army, and they do not accept anyone other than themselves reaching it. What made matters worse was that at the beginning of his arrival at the presidency of the Republic he received female students protesting against their being prevented from entering university because of wearing the khimar, and he sympathised with them... All this hastened the wrath of the secularists and the army.

Özal had founded the Motherland Party and won public opinion, because he appeared to the people, and especially the people of the villages, to be standing in the ranks of Islam, which they profess, in confronting the secularism carried by the men of the army. He came to work with skill, with America's help, and almost succeeded in weakening the authority of the army by creating parallel military forces, but he died, or was killed by a conspiracy against him by the secularists, the creatures of the English, as some news leaked at the time.

Second: After that, government became unstable for any one side. The men of the English work in the political arena, and so do the Americans. The army began to arrange the situation of the Motherland Party (Özal's party), so they brought Mesut Yılmaz to its chairmanship, and the party became loyal to the English, because Mesut Yılmaz is one of their men. He expelled Özal's group from the party. In return, the elements that had been expelled from the Motherland Party for their loyalty to Özal and America joined the Welfare Party, because of their Islamic inclinations, and they came to have a strong influence in Erbakan's party, and America's scale became the weightier in it, even though Erbakan was closer to the men of the English. This is what made the coalition government in the nineties, made up of the True Path Party (Çiller), loyal to America, and the Welfare Party (Erbakan), which was influenced by the entry of Özal's elements into it, appear as though it were being steered by America. The army feared America's return to holding power as it had been in Özal's era, so the army intervened, ended the coalition government and seized power. That was on 28 February 1997, and this incident entered history under the name of the 28 February movement. Among its first actions was that it turned to the Welfare Party and dissolved it, and it was re-formed under the name of the Virtue Party after all of America's group had been expelled from it, whether those who had joined it from Özal's party or those who were originally in it but went along with America, such as Abdullah Gül and Erdoğan. After the collapse of the coalition government, the army entrusted Bülent Ecevit with forming the government. He is one of the pillars of English policy in Turkey, and his wife is of the Dönmeh Jews. He formed a coalition government with the party of Mesut Yılmaz, leader of the Motherland Party, which had come to go along with the English. Thus the secularists of the English returned to holding government after the incident of 28 February.

Third: It became clear to America that directly confronting the army is a difficult matter and creating a parallel force is a matter fraught with dangers, so it saw another method: to work to exclude the army by way of (democracy), by bringing one of its men to government with a parliamentary majority, so that he could legislate laws that limit the authority of the army. And so it was. Its choice fell on Erdoğan and Gül, who had been expelled from the Virtue Party after the incident of 28 February and had begun working with their circles, and they formed the Justice and Development Party under the chairmanship of Erdoğan. He has attributes similar to Özal: Erdoğan is Sufi in his tariqah, and Islamic sentiments appear on him although he is secular, and he is one of America's men, loyal to it, for he has gone along with it since his mayoralty of Istanbul. Despite his judicial prosecution by the army because of the poem he composed, and his political harassment, he remained active in his loyalty to America and in working in this direction.

After that the preparation of the stage for Erdoğan's arrival began. America withdrew (5-7) billion dollars from the Turkish Central Bank in 2001, since the economic privileges whose foundations were laid in Özal's period enabled America to carry out this operation with ease and simplicity. It created an economic shock, and the people's discontent began, because the purchasing power of the lira fell sharply, and the people's resentment of Ecevit and his government increased.

Meanwhile America managed to penetrate a small party that was in coalition with Yılmaz's party and Ecevit's party, namely the Nationalist Movement Party under the chairmanship of Devlet Bahçeli, and prompted it to demand early elections and to threaten to resign if the elections did not take place. Thus early elections were announced for 3/11/2002. When the secularists of the English could not postpone the elections, they moved the Cem Uzan business group, one of the financial pillars of the (English) secularists, to carry out an intensive negative campaign regarding the election of the Justice Party, during which Uzan spent millions of dollars in a relatively short period. Nevertheless, the Justice and Development Party won the elections with a crushing victory, especially since in its electoral propaganda it mixed secularism with a little of an Islamic touch; but, little as it was, it attracted the votes of the general Muslims to it, because of the provocative hostility to Islam they had met from the secularists of the army and the Kemalists. Thus it won and secured the parliamentary majority, and formed the government alone. The opposition party facing it in parliament was a section that split from Ecevit under the name of (the Republican People's Party - Deniz Baykal), while Ecevit's party remained under the name of the Democratic Left Party. When Erdoğan reached power he dealt a knockout blow to the Uzan group, which had done its utmost so that the Justice Party would not win, accusing the group of corruption... and all their properties came into the circle of the judiciary.

Fourth: Erdoğan began implementing the drawn-up plan of strengthening ties with America and weakening the influence of the English, and especially the army. Among his first actions was that he presented to parliament a law reducing the power of the National Security Council to intervene in government, and likewise making the Council mixed, of military and civilian members. The army was irritated by that, to the extent that some news leaked that the (military) were behind the Istanbul bombings at the end of 2003 CE, in order to create a security disruption that they could exploit to intervene, like the earlier February movement, but they did not succeed in that. Then the next step was the signing of the shared vision document between the Turkish government and the government of the United States, which Abdullah Gül signed with Rice on 05/07/2006. Its broad lines, as they appeared in the press statement published on 05/07/2006 on the official website of the American State Department, came beginning with an introduction in which it said: «We share values and thoughts relating to regional and global aims: the development of peace, democracy, freedoms, prosperity». After the introduction, the broad lines were mentioned, and we set down here the headings of those lines:

((The United States and Turkey pledge to work together on all the following issues:

- "Developing peace and stability through the democratic path in the Broader Middle East".
- "Supporting global efforts aimed at bringing about a lasting solution to the Arab-'Israeli' conflict, and global efforts aimed at bringing about a lasting solution to the Palestinian-'Israeli' conflict based on two states".
- "Supporting the development of stability, democracy and prosperity in a united Iraq".
- "Supporting diplomatic efforts regarding the Iranian nuclear programme and (5P+1)".
- "Contributing to bringing about stability, democracy and prosperity in the region of the Black Sea, the Caucasus, Central Asia and Afghanistan".
- "Supporting the final, integrated, comprehensive solution, satisfactory to both sides, under the auspices of the United Nations with regard to the Cyprus issue, and ending the boycott imposed on Turkish Northern Cyprus".
- "Raising the level of security around energy sources through diversifying sources and lines, including the lines coming from the Caspian Sea".
- "Strengthening relations with the Atlantic Ocean region (across the Atlantic Ocean) and the changes in the NATO alliance".
- "Fighting terrorism and its offshoots, including the Kurdistan Workers' Party".
- "Preventing the spread of weapons of mass destruction".
- "Prohibiting the smuggling of: people, weapons, drugs".
- "Raising the level of understanding, respect and appreciation between religions and cultures and within them".
- "Developing and supporting continuous, effective and joint works that serve to find solutions to crises that form a shared concern, and to international challenges".

Fifth: As for the Kurdistan Workers' Party and its role with the army and the government:

1 - The party was founded in 1979, but it actually emerged at America's direction in 1984, in Özal's era (1983 - 1993), when it carried out its first operation against the army in Siirt (a Kurdish city in the east of Turkey). It was intended by this to put pressure on the army in terms of security, simultaneously with Özal's pressure on the army militarily by establishing (a police force armed with strong, heavy armament), which continued in Özal's era until the end of his era, when the army confiscated the heavy weapons belonging to the security apparatuses.

The situation of the Workers' Party continued in this manner, as a security weapon in America's hand in the face of the Turkish army, until the end of 1997 and the beginning of 1998, when two factors appeared:

The first: the movement of 28 February 1997, which returned to government Ecevit, England's veteran man, and he became prime minister, and he came declaring in his programme the decisive elimination of the Kurdistan Workers' Party.

The second: the Turkish threats to Syria of declaring war on it, saying (Syria is waging an undeclared war on Turkey through their support for the Workers' Party). Then Turkey announced that it would respond to this undeclared Syrian war, and one of Turkey's generals declared: (We are able to enter Syria from one side and exit from its other side). The matter became seriously critical, so America decided, first, in order to preserve Syria's remaining under its influence; second, out of its realisation of the failure of the security method in penetrating Turkey; and third, of the necessity of changing this method to political work with the concepts of democracy, freedom and human rights... in Turkey, it decided to conclude a deal with the Turkish army by way of the new Turkish government, since the political and military authority in Turkey had become of one kind, by giving up the Kurdistan Workers' Party as a (military) organisation and ending the crisis with Syria. And so it was, as this was reflected on Syria, and calming talks took place between Turkey and Syria, crowned by the conclusion of the Adana Agreement in October 1998. According to the agreement, Syria accepted to stop its support for the Kurdistan Workers' Party, to expel Abdullah Öcalan and to hand over a number of the other leaders in Syria to Turkey.

Öcalan left Syria for Russia, which refused him asylum, so he left it for Greece, then Italy, then he came to settle in Kenya, where a unit of the special forces of the Turkish army went to Kenya and received him, by arrangement of American intelligence.

After that America became active in political, popular and democratic work... until it succeeded in bringing Erdoğan and his party to government in 2002, as we explained earlier.

As for the Kurdistan Workers' Party, it split: one section went according to the new American method of work, that is, towards political work, under the leadership of Osman Öcalan; and a section that the English took hold of, most of whose leaders are of Jewish origin, and this section came under the wing of the Turkish army. This section, under the leadership of Zübeyir Aydar, came to be exploited in creating unrest against Erdoğan's government loyal to America, and at the same time in creating a justification for the army to impose its presence whenever necessary, on the pretext of eliminating the unrest. Thus American policy with regard to the Workers' Party, and especially in the era of the Justice Party government, is that the issue of the Kurds be a political issue, whereas English policy with regard to the Workers' Party, and especially in the era of the Justice Party government, is that the issue of the Kurds be a security issue, that is, the reverse of what the situation was before the Adana Agreement. This explains the armed actions that the Kurdistan Workers' Party, the English wing, is launching at the present time.

Sixth: Through the (democratic) actions that the Justice Party carried out, America was able to cross the red lines on which the Kemalist secularists do not keep silent.

The army, which counts itself the protector of Kemalist secularism, holds the reins of affairs in the country by means of four things in the institutions of the state, which it does not allow to be infiltrated:

The first: the office of the presidency of the Republic. Even if it is at present closer to being a moral symbol of the state, they consider it the (Atatürkist) colouring of the state.

The second: the Constitutional Court, by means of which they hold the legal justification for military intervention and for annulling the laws that they count as violating the constitution, according to their interests.

The third: the institution of education, which is important to them for controlling the culture of the generations.

The fourth: the National Security Council, by means of which they hold the security justification for military intervention.

What has happened is that the government of the Justice and Development Party, by using democratic means and legislating laws in the Chamber of Deputies, was able to infiltrate the Constitutional Court with two of its men at present. The judges of the court number (11), two of them not supporters of the army, and the government is continuing in this field.

And in the National Security Council it was able to bring in something close to an equal division between military men and civilians.

It tried, and is still trying, with regard to the institution of higher education (YÖK), and although it has not been able to infiltrate it in any weighty way until now, it is continuing in that.

Until now the Justice Party government had been content with working in the previous three fields, but today it has extended to the presidency of the Republic, and this symbol is important and sensitive for the army, the protectors of the secular system. The government tried, by democratic methods, since they have the majority in parliament, to bring Abdullah Gül to the presidency. However, the army considered this matter a crossing of the greatest of the red lines, so it rose up strongly in the face of it, using methods of threat and menace side by side with democratic methods... Therefore it mobilised its masses from every place to move secular public opinion, and at the same time it issued a statement in the name of the General Staff at 23:15 on the night of Friday 27/04/2007, the day on which the Turkish parliament met to hold the first session for electing Abdullah Gül as President of the Republic, in which two thirds were not present, which pushed the Republican People's Party to object to the session and file a suit with the Constitutional Court. It issued a statement bearing the character of a military memorandum through the official website of the General Staff on the internet. The statement was announced in a strange manner the like of which had not happened at any previous time, as the media circles were informed to consult the website of the General Staff on the internet. The most important thing the statement focused on was: "The problem whose priority has appeared in recent days concerning the presidency of the Republic centres on making secularism a subject of debate. This situation has been viewed by the Turkish Armed Forces with grave concern. It must not be forgotten that the Turkish Armed Forces are the protector of secularism, and they are against this debate and these negative remarks. Therefore the Turkish Armed Forces will place their weight and their method at the appropriate time in a clear and evident manner, and this is something no one may doubt." In the last paragraph of the statement came an open threat hinting at a military coup: "In summary, whoever stands in the face of the slogan 'How happy is the one who says I am a Turk', which the founder of the Republic, the revered Atatürk, laid down for us, is an enemy of the Turkish Republic and will remain so. The Turkish Armed Forces maintain their unshakeable determination (decision) in carrying out their declared duties legally granted to them with regard to preserving these attributes (the attributes of the Republic and the foundations on which it stands), and their attachment to and belief in this determination is absolute."

This statement was, for the secularists who were discontented with the presence of the Justice and Development Party in government, since they were unable to do anything but watch, a factor of confidence that the army is able to threaten and not merely to watch and stand as a spectator. Therefore, after the statement/memorandum was issued, the extent of the (arrogance) and strength that seized the secular circles became visible.

Had it not been that America and the government charged the atmosphere with «democracy» and «the rejection of coups», and the exploitation of the atmosphere of the European Union negotiations, freedoms and human rights... which helped make the circumstances prevent or limit military coups, had it not been for that, the army would have carried out a coup, as was customary in the past.

In view of the government's realisation of that, it did not let the General Staff's statement pass peacefully. Rather, at 15:00 on 28/04/2007 it issued a strongly worded press statement responding to what came in the military statement/memorandum, and in its press statement came striking expressions such as "The Chief of the General Staff of the Turkish Armed Forces is, from the legislative point of view, under the command/authority of the Prime Minister," and the like. The government wanted to spoil for the army its (arrogance) contained in its military statement, and to make it feel that its threat was a moral threat and not an actual threat, for it does not have the capability to carry out a military coup as in former days. The government's statement was also a message of rehabilitation for the party's bases, which had been shaken following the issuing of the army's statement/memorandum, so it suggested to these bases that the government was still able to stand. Nevertheless, the government realised that the decision of the Constitutional Court would be on the side of the army's demand to annul the session, since the court is made up of the men of the English except for two. And so it was: on the suit that the Republican People's Party filed, the court's decision was issued on 01 May 2007 annulling the first round of the election of the President of the Republic, and the condition was approved that two thirds of the deputies must be present in each round of the three electoral rounds.

Erdoğan and those around him had declared at first that they respect the decision of the Constitutional Court; however, after they studied the reality of the situation, they showed their fury at the decision, having felt the severity of the slap directed at them. The most prominent thing in that was what Erdoğan declared when he described the decision as "a bullet fired at democracy". Erdoğan's attempt to retreat, by saying that his statement had not been directed at the Constitutional Court but at the chairman of the Republican People's Party Deniz Baykal, who had been seeking to stir up the court, did not lessen the effect of the statement!

Nevertheless, Erdoğan did not (surrender). Rather, he made a statement on 01/05, following the announcement of the court's decision, in which he announced that he would present a draft resolution to the Chamber of Deputies for electing the President of the Republic directly by the people, detailing that as follows:

- Making constitutional amendments enabling the people to elect the President of the Republic by direct election, and not as is happening now, where it takes place by way of parliament.

- Making changes to the term of the presidency of the Republic, from one term lasting seven years to two terms, each term lasting five years.

- Making changes relating to the general elections so that they become once every four years, and not as is happening now, where the general elections are held every five years.

- Making changes in the age of the deputy, so that one may become a deputy on reaching 25 years instead of the 30 years currently in force.

- Reducing the number of deputies who must be present for all sessions of parliament, including the session for electing the President of the Republic, from two thirds to a majority only.

The most important articles contained within the constitutional reforms/changes that Erdoğan declared are enabling the people to elect the President of the Republic by direct election, in addition to reducing the number of deputies who must be present for all sessions of parliament from two thirds to a majority.

Thus Erdoğan presented a draft to parliament with these proposals. And because their approval in parliament needs two thirds, that is (367) deputies, while the Justice Party holds the majority but does not hold two thirds, the search therefore began to secure this number. So it turned towards the Motherland Party, which holds twenty deputies, and by agreement with it two thirds would be provided.

The Motherland Party is the one that Özal founded, but after the incident of his killing the army carried out a campaign of tearing the party apart and getting rid of its hostile elements, and it gave its chairmanship to Mesut Yılmaz, where the loyalty is to the army (the English). When the party was defeated in the elections of 2002 CE, in which the Justice Party won, Mesut Yılmaz resigned from the chairmanship of the party because of his defeat. After that the Motherland Party entered a crisis of leadership, until (Erkan Mumcu) came to head it. He was a famous former member of the Motherland Party in the era of Mesut Yılmaz, who had resigned from it and entered the elections of 2002 under the name of the Justice and Development Party and not under the name of the Motherland Party, and so he became a member of parliament for the Justice Party and then held the post of Minister of Tourism. When the leadership crisis in the Motherland Party became acute, and on the basis of negotiations with him over the chairmanship of the party, he resigned from membership of the Justice Party and went back to the Motherland Party as chairman. Despite his previous entry into the elections on the lists of the Justice Party, he was not able to support the Justice Party in the voting session for the election of Gül to the presidency, because of the pressure of Mesut Yılmaz's group in the Motherland Party, owing to the English background of this group. Had he done so with his twenty deputies, the quorum of two thirds would have been achieved in the election of Gül to the presidency.

In the wake of that, the circles that had elected him when he stood on the lists of the Justice Party became resentful of him, and considered his conduct in not taking part in the vote a stab in the back. And because the parliamentary elections had come to the door (22 July 2007), he therefore used his powers as chairman of the party and persuaded the party's administration to vote in favour of the Justice Party's draft on the election of the president by the people, out of keenness to win in the coming elections and to placate the public of the Justice Party that had elected him previously. Thus the Justice Party's draft for electing the president by the people succeeded in parliament by securing the quorum of two thirds, in the parliament's vote dated 10/5/2007.

This was another attempt to harass the army and the secularists of the English, because the secular republic, ever since it was founded in Turkey, has not been able to market itself to the Muslim people, who have never ceased to refuse to adopt the method on which it proceeds. Despite using all kinds of severity and oppression with an iron fist to make the people accept this system and adopt it, and despite its carrying out four military coups during nearly fifty years from the political opening following the Second World War until now, despite that, it has not been able to make this Muslim people embrace it and adopt it in any form whatsoever. For this reason the army and the secularists of the English do not accept that the president be elected by the people, nor that those constitutional amendments be approved at this time. Therefore they resorted to their last line of defence, which is the need of the law issued by parliament with two thirds for the signature of Sezer for it to become effective. It is known that Sezer, who reached the presidency of the Republic in 2000 CE, came from the Constitutional Court, for he was its president. Therefore they expect that he will exploit this power given to him (the signature) to the greatest extent possible: either to not pass the law, or to amend it. Although the president has the right of objection only twice, he has other means of obstruction, such as returning the subject to the Constitutional Court with legal arrangements for which the lawyers, with their (tricks), are able to find ways in or ways out; or, if matters become tight for him, the army may resort to the Workers' Party, the English wing, to create a security escalation that the army exploits in creating a state of military emergency affecting the course of the presidential elections, whether directly by the people or by returning once again to the Chamber of Deputies if Erdoğan's reform project fails... In return, the efforts of the government and America will not stay silent over any legal opportunity made available to them...; that is, the conflict is a hot conflict in which each team uses the utmost of the weapons it has.

Seventh: After that, matters proceeded as follows:

1 - The decision of the Chamber of Deputies on the reforms and on the election of the president directly by the people was submitted to the President of the Republic, and the president rejected it and returned it to parliament after fifteen days, which is the period allowed to him under the law.

2 - Parliament met on 29/5/2007 and once again approved the draft for the second time, and it obtained (369) votes, as the Motherland Party voted with it; that is, it obtained the required two-thirds majority for the second time.

3 - Then the draft was returned to the President of the Republic. Now, after this second time, the President of the Republic cannot reject it and return it. Rather, he must either approve it, or resort to a referendum on it, but by (crooked) ways so as to guarantee the failure of the referendum, or resort to a way out through the Constitutional Court, or create a state of military emergency by contriving military actions, exploiting the actions of the English wing in the Workers' Party, and especially those who rely on Masoud Barzani in Iraq, who has an English background.

Signs of the military movements that the news has recently carried have appeared within this context. Bombings took place in the east of Ankara on 22/5/2007, which the army attributed to the Kurdistan Workers' Party, causing the killing of seven people; then about 60 thousand soldiers were massed with heavy weapons including tanks, and it is escalating, heading for the border with Iraq (Kurdistan). The army magnified the matter in order to influence the atmosphere of the coming elections, especially by its carrying out military manoeuvres in the neighbouring Turkish province of Şırnak on 7/6/2007 using tank shells. However, the government's position was trying to calm things in order to get the elections through in a calm atmosphere. That is, the army and the government are in a hot manoeuvre: the army is trying military escalation and magnifying the danger of the Workers' Party to the entity of the state, trying by that to embarrass the government in order to create political cover for a tense military situation, which would make the priority of the parliamentary and presidential elections slip back and keep the current situation in the hand of the army. The government is trying to lessen the excess of the army and to lower the ceiling of the Workers' Party's danger, while at the same time trying not to appear uninterested in the security of the country, and so on and so forth. As for America, on the other side, it insists on the Turkish army not intervening in Kurdistan; indeed, beyond that, its aircraft crossed the Turkish border while monitoring the Turkish army's massing, and its position was (deflating) for the military action of the Turkish army. This made the Turkish Chief of Staff Yaşar Büyükanıt enraged at this position, and he declared on 31/5/2007, saying: [(Some allies) of our country are providing assistance to the Kurdish rebels in the Anatolia region], adding during a seminar in Istanbul: (Those who give us lessons in human rights support «terrorism»), as the French news agency reported, and as the Turkish television channel NTV broadcast. The American Secretary of Defense responded to that indirectly in a speech he delivered at a security conference held in Singapore on 3/6/2007, drawing the attention of the Turkish army to not carrying out any military action on the Iraqi border.

What is expected is that Sezer will try, by all the means that he and the army are able to use, not to pass the law on the election of the president by the people, for the reasons we mentioned earlier.

The crisis may remain going back and forth until the parliamentary elections are held. If the Justice Party is able to win two thirds, it can then elect the president in parliament; and if it cannot take two thirds, Turkey may continue for a period without (presidential) stability, and the two sides may resort to a consensual solution:

That the army gives up imposing the president it wants.

And that the government gives up the election of the president by the people.

This solution will be no more than a sedative, for the army will not easily accept not installing the president it wants, and since a coup is difficult at present, it may contrive military actions to influence the course of affairs.

Likewise the government will not let an opportunity made available to it pass without benefiting from it.

This means that arriving at a political crisis is an expected matter, unless the Justice Party obtains two thirds by itself in the coming parliamentary elections on 22 July.

Eighth: As for the balance of power in the coming elections, it is as follows:

The weightier view is that three parties will be able to enter parliament, that is, obtain the established percentage of ten per cent and above: they are the Justice and Development Party (AKP), the Republican People's Party (CHP), and the Democratic Party (DP), whose formation the True Path (ANAP) and Motherland (DYP) parties announced by creating a union between them.

As for the Justice Party, it will win the majority, and it may obtain two thirds if it is able to show itself to the people as (wronged), and that the English secularists did not enable it to elect the President of the Republic with its majority in parliament, and likewise that they refused (Sezer's refusal to sign the election of the president by the people, with the knowledge that the law was issued by the deputies with two thirds, and that, and that... in addition to the political and economic actions with which America supports it...; then if it is able to treat its exposure before the Islamic milieu that elected it the first time, since it became clear to this milieu that the Justice Party did nothing Islamic for them, not even the khimar, whose ban it was unable to remove...; I say, if it is able to master these methods, it may win two thirds. However, what has appeared recently, of removing those of Islamic orientation from the lists of candidates to please the secularists, will affect the party's percentage of victory.

As for the Republican People's Party, it will not face a problem in passing the electoral threshold (10%) to enter parliament. However, the number of seats it will be able to obtain in parliament will depend on its ability to build an electoral alliance (as the army wants) with the Democratic Left Party (DSP) and the rest of the other leftist parties, that is, that the People's Party return to what it was previously before Deniz Baykal's split from Ecevit. However, what obstructs that is Rahşan Ecevit (the wife of Bülent Ecevit and the moral chairwoman of the Democratic Left Party); but the weightier view is that she aims to delay the agreement, not to prevent it. Her aim in that is to move public opinion towards the Democratic Left Party, by way of publicity for it, and likewise so that she can bargain with the Republican People's Party from a position of strength over the sharing of the seats the union obtains in the elections. Although the Republican People's Party agreed to give the Democratic Left Party twenty parliamentary seats, there are sixty party officials in the Democratic Left Party who aspire to be members of parliament! In any case, if the army is able to restore the bond between the two wings that split from each other, their fortune will be relatively great, and it will be at the expense of the two thirds that the Justice Party hopes to obtain.

As for the new union of the True Path and Motherland parties under the name of the Democratic Party, which is the name of Adnan Menderes's former party, which they chose as a name for themselves by way of a dramatic tactic to tickle the people's sentiments, this union will most likely not go beyond an electoral alliance, for it resembles the parties that are based on passing occasions. This union is expected to pass the required percentage and consequently enter parliament. That is, if the union of these two parties remains in place (a crack has recently appeared in this union while it is at the beginning of its course; accordingly, if the crack becomes a separation, the chance of each party on its own will weaken strikingly).

After that come other parties with a lesser likelihood:

The Nationalist Movement Party (MHP): it is expected to reach the electoral threshold and to be the fourth of the political parties that will be able to enter parliament, if it is able to employ the operations of the Kurdistan Workers' Party in the interest of moving the nationalist and patriotic sentiments among the people; otherwise it may not reach the percentage that enables it to enter parliament.

The party of the Kurds called the Democratic Society Party (DTP): it is unlikely that it will reach the required percentage, because its supporters and those who vote for it do not exceed 7% according to the estimates of those who are informed. And because it realises that, it is trying to take part in the elections by way of independent candidates.

The Great Union Party (BBP) and Erbakan's party, the Felicity Party (SP), which address the Islamic milieu: unless they ally with each other, it is unlikely that either of them will obtain the established percentage.

It is worth mentioning that any military, security, economic or political developments that occur will change the data mentioned above.

Whatever the matter may be, the Kemalist English secularists and the American secularists, who wrap their secularism in some Islamic (touches), are all now in a whirlpool of actual conflict. This is the nature of states controlled by a military authority and a political authority that differ in loyalty, for these states face two kinds of political crisis:

1 - The crisis of coalition governments: In this case, either the crisis is between the coalition partners because of one or more disagreements between them, or there is a crisis of lack of understanding between the coalition government and the army. If it is between the coalition partners and cannot be remedied, the government scatters and falls, and the crisis ends with the building of a new government or by heading to the ballot boxes to hold early elections. And if it is between the coalition government and the army and cannot be remedied, then a coup or military intervention occurs, as happened in the white military coup of 28 February 1997, and in the military coups that preceded it in 1960, 1971 and 1980.

2 - The crisis of a single-party government: In this case, either the ruling party contains an internal crisis that appears in a split within the party, or the crisis is between the single-party government and the army. If it arises from within the party and cannot be remedied, the crisis ends with the ending of the negative factors within the party, or by way of the party splitting upon itself, so that the stronger section forms a new government or heads towards holding early elections. And if it is between the single-party government and the army, this is one of the most dangerous crises, and it will be accompanied by a hot conflict leading to a military coup, unless pressing domestic and international circumstances on the army prevent that. This is the current crisis, since it is between the single-party government (the Justice and Development Party) and the army and its followers. This crisis will remain interacting hotly until a new balance of power appears, or the current balance of power is entrenched, according to the army's ability to carry out military manoeuvring to create emergency conditions, or the government's ability to exploit the international circumstances to thwart the military emergency conditions that the army is trying to create.

In summary:

1 - The reality of what is going on is a hot conflict between the Kemalist secularists of the English, at their head the army, to preserve the position of the president in their hand, to try to regain hold of the National Security Council and to preserve the Constitutional Court from infiltration; and the secularists of America, who wrap their secularism in some Islamic (touches) to attract the general Muslims, in view of the English secularists' hostility to Islam in a manner provocative to the sentiments of the Muslims, in order to weaken the army's (the English) control over the joints of power in Turkey, to continue widening the government's intervention in the National Security Council, and hence to create openings, even narrow ones, for entering the (fortress) of the English in the army, along with widening the number of the government's men in the Constitutional Court and excluding the army's control in holding the President of the Republic.

2 - The Kurdistan Workers' Party is split into two wings: an English wing exploited by the army to heat up the atmosphere in terms of security when the army needs to create a state of military emergency as a result of its being cornered politically by the government, in order to move the issue to the military side, as is happening now in the massing of the Turkish army in the direction of the Iraqi border.

As for the second wing, it is with America, and its current broad line is that the issue remain political, in harmony with the American line of the government's course.

3 - The matter of the presidency of the state will most likely remain pending until after the early parliamentary elections on 22/7/2007, and in the light of their results the matter of the presidential elections will be settled.

On 22 Jumada al-Ula 1428 AH.
